steps.full:
Both additional framings route to the same two existing nodes and surface nothing holding the temperature–mass law. My picture is now complete enough to decide.

**Analysis.** The candidate at 0.966 ("Black holes emit Hawking radiation") is the bare emission claim. The source text in front of me asserts that plus the quantitative law (T ∝ 1/M). These differ at the granularity §2 names explicitly: the temperature law is a *specification* of the emission claim, and different considerations bear on it — the derivation of the Hawking temperature formula, its exact proportionality, whether the spectrum is strictly thermal — none of which bears on the bare existence question. An argument for emission does not establish the 1/M scaling without further work, and vice versa. So not a match. The evaporation node is a downstream consequence of the law (small mass → high temperature → fast evaporation), not a counterpart. No node in the graph holds the law itself; searching under six framings including the negation turned up nothing closer than the two candidates above.

This is a settled, textbook-level result, which affects effort, not identity: the node is still worth minting so instances of the quantitative statement aggregate on their own proposition rather than blurring into the emission node. The proposed canonical form is serviceable: neutral, affirmative, fifteen words, fair to any speaker on either side, and its descriptive (unnamed) wording keeps it visibly distinct from the emission node's text. Direction: the discourse poses Hawking's result as a positive thesis, so the affirmative form is right; the source asserts it outright, so the stance is "affirms".
